question: Should an ambiguous outbound delivery with no reconciliation-capable adapter remain pending indefinitely without consuming retry budget, or should it become terminal and visibly failed after a bounded period?
rationale: The code cannot determine whether the platform committed the send, so either choice intentionally trades duplicate-delivery risk against stranded-message and unbounded-pending-state risk; repository policy requires an owner to choose that product contract.

options.title: Retain Pending With Follow-Up
options.body: Land the narrow no-budget retention policy and keep operator visibility, durable receipts, and adapter reconciliation tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87544.

options.title: Dead-Letter At A Bound
options.body: Preserve a bounded terminal transition for unreconcilable rows and require health or session surfacing so users can recover manually.

options.title: Add Explicit Blocked State
options.body: Pause this PR and introduce a distinct awaiting-reconciliation state with dedicated health, doctor, or UI semantics before changing the terminal policy.

recommendation.title: Retain Pending With Follow-Up
recommendation.body: Land the narrow no-budget retention policy and keep operator visibility, durable receipts, and adapter reconciliation tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87544.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged outbound-recovery rewrite defines the current lifecycle and makes them the strongest history-based routing candidate for this policy choice.
